questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.

Raman's discovery, made __during the voyaging over__ the Mediterranean sea, that water molecules could scatter light just like air molecules, was very radical in those days.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. during a voyage across.

 
• The underlined part of the sentence is incorrect and has to be substituted with another phrase.
 
• The **noun ‘voyage**: a long journey involving travel by sea or in space’ has to be used here instead of the verb ‘voyaging: go on a voyage’.
 
• Option 4 is the correct answer since it:
 
 
• uses the **correct indefinite article “a**- used with a singular count noun when you mean "one of many", "any", "in general”.
 
• uses the **correct noun ‘voyage’**.
 
• uses the **correct preposition ‘across**: from one side to the other of (a place, area, etc.)’.
 
 
 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• Option 1- the preposition ‘above: extending upwards over’ is used wrongly here.
 
• Option 3- the indefinite article ‘an’ should only be used in front of words starting with a vowel or words that sound like they start with a vowel.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the ways for confirming the authenticity of the chapter?

options.text: The name of the writer was inscribed on it as also on the earlier chapters.
The slip used by the manuscript writer was similar to the slips on other chapters
The binding cover was of the same colour
The handwriting matched that of the other chapters

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

 
• The chapters written by Fujiwara no Teika were already authenticated. The recently found chapter had certain similarities to Teika’s other chapters.

 
 
• At the very end of the passage, it is written that the handwriting in the recently found chapter matched the one found in the other authenticated chapters.
 
• The recently found chapter also had blue binding which matched the binding of the others.
 
• There was also a small slip of paper kept by Teika in front of the chapter. The other chapters also had these slips.
 
 
 
• **Nowhere in the entire passage** it is said that the **name of the writer was inscribed** on the recently found chapter as also on the earlier chapters.
 
• Hence option 1 was not one of the ways for confirming the authenticity of the chapter.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Educators have ______ unique responsibility towards the empowerment of their students.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. a.

 
• Here, ‘responsibility’ is considered as a **singular countable noun**. 
 
• We have to use the indefinite article ‘a’ before ‘unique responsibility’ since ‘unique’ sounds as if it starts with ‘Y’. ‘A unique responsibility’ means** ‘one unique responsibility’**.

​The other options are cancelled because: 

 
• ‘U’ is a vowel word, but while pronouncing “unique” it sounds as if it starts with ‘Y’ which is not a vowel. So we cannot use 'an'.
 
• 'Some' is used with plural countable nouns and uncountable nouns i.e. if we don't know the exact amount of something or if we use nouns we cannot count, e.g. liquids.
 
• 'Few’ is used to denote a small number of something. It is only used with plural countable nouns.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.**

The vibrations from wind instruments ______ always positive and good ______ your breathing and health.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. are; for. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• According to the **Subject-Verb Agreement rule**, the subject and verb must agree in number. This means both need to be singular or both need to be plural.
 
• **‘The vibrations****’ is a plural subject.** So the verb that accompanies it must be plural too. This helps to cancel out options 1 and 3.
 
• Now option 4 is left. 'Were' is a plural verb but 'to' is the incorrect preposition here. Some instances where 'to' is used are given below:
 
 
• Destination- I’m going to Europe.
 
• Distance- It’s about five miles from my house to the church.
 
• Comparing- I prefer sleeping to exercising.
 
• Giving- He gave the apple to his sister.
 
• Motive- He came here to see you.
 
 
 
• Meanwhile, **‘for’ here is used while stating the benefit of something.** An example of using ‘for’ for this is: *Vitamin C is good for your health. *
 
• Hence we have to use **‘are’(plural verb)** in the first blank and **‘for’(correct preposition)** in the second blank.

**The correct sentence is: ***The vibrations from wind instruments **are** always positive and good **for **your breathing and health.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.solution:

• ‘Its’ is the appropriate possessive pronoun to be used. It means “belonging to or **associated with a thing previously mentioned** or easily identified.”

• Their- belonging to or associated with the people or things previously mentioned or easily identified. Eg: The parents dropped their kids off at school.
 
• Our- belonging to or associated with the speaker and one or more other people previously mentioned or easily identified. Eg: "Jo and I had our hair cut."
 
 
 
• These pronouns can only be used for living things.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.

The World Health Organisation warned the Government __that even many people were likely__ to die of epidemics than of the tsunami.

options.text: that so many people are likely
that even most people are going to be likely

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. that more people were likely.

The underlined part of the sentence is incorrect and has to be substituted with another phrase.

 
• We can understand from the given sentence in the question that the WHO warned the government of more deaths in the case of epidemics than a tsunami. 
 
• Option 4 is the correct answer since:
 
 
• Notice the word ‘than’. It helps to introduce the second element in a comparison. So compared to a tsunami, epidemics cause more deaths. In a general sense, more is used when referring to a greater or additional amount or degree.
 
• The correct verb ‘were’ which is the past tense of ‘be’ is used here. 
 
 
 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• Option 1- the verb ‘are’ which is present tense of ‘be’ is wrongly used here. The structure of the sentence is in past tense. 
 
• Option 3- ‘Most’ is used when referring to the greatest in amount or degree. It is incorrect to use that here as it indicates that epidemics cause the greatest amount of deaths which is untrue. The verb tense ‘are going’ is in the present tense, which is also incorrect.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

I tried to contact my dentist but her cell phone __appeared to have been__ switched off.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. No improvement.

 
• The underlined part of the sentence is correct and doesn’t have to be substituted with another phrase.
 
• Look at the given sentence in this way: I tried to contact my dentist but her cell phone appeared to have been switched off (by her). This sentence is in the **passive voice**.
 
 
• The **active voice** of this will be: I tried to contact my dentist but she appears to have switched off her cell phone.
 
• The active voice emphasizes the person or agent who performs an action (here it’s the dentist), in short, the “actor.” The **passive voice emphasizes the recipient of the action** or sometimes the action itself (here it’s the **cell phone**).
 
• Eg: Active voice- The dog chased the ball. Passive voice- The ball was chased by the dog.
 
 
 
• The verb tense (have + switched off) when the sentence is in the active voice is **present perfect tense**. 
 
 
• The present perfect tense refers to an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past or began in the past and continued to the present time. 
 
• This tense is formed by have/has + the past participle.
 
• In the present perfect tense we make **passive verb forms** by putting has/have + been before the past participle form of the verb. This is what is given in the question- have been + switched off.
 
• Eg: Active voice- I have finished (present perfect) the pudding. Passive voice- The pudding has been finished (passive form of present perfect) by me. 
 
 
 
• The rest of the given options are grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Chinese leader's formal Chinese suit ______ Changpao.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. is called. 

The sentence can be considered as “The Chinese leader's formal Chinese suit is called Changpao (by someone).” 

 
• This sentence is written in the passive voice.
 
• The passive voice is used when we want to focus attention on the person or thing affected by the action, here the thing is the Chinese suit.

The active voice will be “(Someone) calls(simple present tense) the Chinese leader’s formal suit Changpao.” 

 
• We use the simple present tense for anything that is factual.
 
• When active verb is in the simple present tense (calls), we make passive verb forms with is/am/are + past participle form of the verb (is called). 

​Other options are incorrect because:

 
• Option 1- ​‘Call’ is a base verb and base form of verbs can only be directly used after 

 
 
• modal auxiliaries like can, may, must, would, should, could etc.
 
• Why- eg: Why stay? 
 
 
 
• Option 2- According to the Subject-Verb Agreement rule, the subject and verb must agree in number. This means both need to be singular or both need to be plural.
 
 
• ‘Formal Chinese suit’ is a singular subject. 
 
• So the verb that accompanies it must be singular too. 
 
 
 
• Option 3- ‘Will be called Changpao’ means that the name has not been given to the formal suit yet, and this will happen in the future. This is wrong as this piece of clothing was introduced to China during the Qing dynasty (17th–20th centuries).

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Vini bought two new dresses but either is suitable for the festival.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. either is.

 
• The error is in the third segment of the sentence and it has to be modified.
 
• Notice the **conjunction ‘but’** used in the middle of the sentence. It is **used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting** with what has already been mentioned.
 
 
• Hence the sentence would mean: Although Vini bought two new dresses, both of them are not suitable to be worn for the festival. 
 
 
 
• The pronoun ‘either’ used in the sentence is incorrect. It means ‘one or the other of two people or things’.
 
• It has to be replaced with ‘neither’. Neither means "not the one and not the other" or "not either." 
 
 
• The following example shows this use: *You can wear **neither** of the dresses to the party* (you cannot wear the one dress, you cannot wear the other dress also).
 
 

Hence the phrase “either is” should be replaced with “neither of them is”.

Correct sentence: Vini bought two new dresses but neither of them is suitable for the festival.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

__Be polite and courteous__ will greatly improve your chances of making friends at your new office.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. Being polite and courteous.

The underlined part of the sentence is grammatically incorrect and has to be substituted with another phrase. 

 
• Notice that whatever comes in the underlined part will be the **Subject** in this sentence. 
 
• The subject of a sentence is the person, place, thing, or idea that is doing or being something. You can find the subject of a sentence if you can find the verb. 
 
• Here, ask the question, "Who or what will greatly improve your chances of making friends at your new office?" and the answer to that question is the subject.
 
• ‘Being polite and courteous’ is a gerund phrase acting as the subject. 
 
 
• The gerund looks exactly the same as a present participle, but they are different. To find gerunds in sentences, just look for a verb + ing that is used as a noun.
 
• The gerund always has the same function as a noun (although it looks like a verb).
 
• The gerund phrase can be used as the subject, complement, or object of a sentence. 
 
• Eg: Eating ice cream on a windy day can be a messy experience if you have long, untamed hair. Eating ice cream on a windy day = subject of the verb can be.
 
 

 
• The other options are wrong as they make the sentence grammatically incorrect.

The correct answer is option 1 i.e. Ignorant. 

Aware means “having knowledge or perception of a situation or fact.”

Let us look at the meanings of the given options:

 
• Ignorant: lacking knowledge, information, or awareness about a particular thing
 
• Resilient: (of a person or animal) able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions
 
• Robust: strong and healthy; vigorous
 
• Impervious: unable to be affected by

Hence, out of the given options, Ignorant is the appropriate antonym of Aware.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. If the sentence has no error, then select 'No error'.**

To whom did you give the packet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. No error

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• As we know that "who" is used for the **subject** of the verb, "whom" is used for the **object**
 
• In the case of** Passive voice- ** it swaps the **subject** and **object; **thus, the usage of the preposition '**to'** is correct because 'whom ' is the object of 'give to'
 
 
• **For e.g.-** Whom I talked **to**. [Here, '**I'** is the **subject** and '**whom'** is the **object** of** 'talked to'**]
 
 
 
• Also, **the subject of the sentence is 'you', the helping verb is 'did', the main verb is 'give', the object of the sentence is 'the packet' and the preposition 'to', the preposition always has a prepositional object, so 'whom' is the prepositional object which is written in the starting of the sentence.**
 
• Hence, the given sentence *is grammatically correct.*

questions.question:
In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

Her sister lives in Pune, one of the major city in Maharashtra.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. one of the major city.

 
• The error is in the third segment of the sentence and it has to be modified.
 
• The phrase **‘one of the’** always has to be **followed by a** **plural noun**. 
 
• There are many major cities in the state of Maharashtra, and Pune is just one of them.

Hence the phrase “one of the major city” should be replaced with “one of the major cities”.

Correct sentence: Her sister lives in Pune, one of the major cities in Maharashtra.
